title: An expanded codebook of human transcription factor DNA-binding specificity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both allele-specific binding (ASB) archives from Zenodo 18224872 (CC-BY-4.0): ChIP-seq 155 per-TF TSVs = 289,657 candidate TF-SNP rows, 10,575 at FDR<0.05; GHT-SELEX 178 TSVs = 11,422 rows, 1,485 at FDR<0.05 (sum 12,060 = paper). 36 identical columns, 0 duplicate (TF, rsID, alt) rows, per-replicate ref/alt read counts present, chr1-22 only. Motif-hit rows: 2,366 concordant + 1,198 discordant = 3,564 (= paper). Computed PWM (position weight matrix) direction accuracy myself: 67.5% on ChIP ASBs with a motif hit, 53.3% on the 7,766 ChIP ASBs with no hit. 53 TFs have >=20 significant ChIP ASBs. Also opened MEX metadata_complete_dataset.tsv (35,982 data slices with Train/Val split) and listed Zenodo 15667805, 17307845, IBIS 14174162/14176443 file sizes; GEO GSE280248 RAW is 308 GB; hg38.2bit is 835 MB (HEAD only).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the 74% (1,682/2,260) PWM concordance applies to strongly motif-disrupting ASBs; that MIXALIME corrects for background allelic dosage; that GHT-SELEX used fragmented HEK293 DNA (from companion paper search snippet); column definitions (documented only by reference to the preprint and the MIXALIME GitHub). I did not download reference genome sequence, peak files or the IBIS models.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo 18224872 downloaded without login, CC-BY-4.0; 2.2 MB and 38 MB zips (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Label is already columns: pref_allele (ref/alt), comb_es (allelic effect size) and fdr_comb_pval per TF-SNP row (checked in files).

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are hg38 coordinates plus ref/alt alleles, not sequences; one 835 MB hg38 reference file (or local slicing) gives every window. One download, not thousands of lookups.

a4_units_stated.note: Read counts, log-scale effect sizes and FDR p-values; no physical units to confuse. Exact scale of comb_es documented only in the MIXALIME docs.

a5_enough_rows.note: 289,657 ChIP-seq + 11,422 GHT-SELEX candidate TF-SNP rows, of which 12,060 are significant ASBs (verified). Per TF it is thinner: 53 TFs with >=20 significant ChIP ASBs.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.9 GB (40 MB ASB tables + 835 MB hg38.2bit)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Tables load in seconds in pandas; sequence windows cut from the reference on CPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 10,575 ChIP + 1,485 GHT-SELEX = 12,060 ASBs, and 3,564 motif-hit ASBs, both exactly as stated in the paper (checked).

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is a statistical test (MIXALIME, a negative-binomial model) on measured allele read counts, not a model prediction. The motif_fc columns are features from Codebook PWMs that were built on the same peaks, so use them only as a baseline, never as input to the label.

B1.why: 333 per-TF TSVs with identical 36 columns concatenate trivially; sequence must be added from hg38 (checked).

B2.why: All TSVs parsed first try in pandas; replicate columns are comma lists, easy to split (checked).

B3.why: Effect sizes from one pipeline (MIXALIME) per assay, already corrected for allelic dosage by authors.

B4.why: No censored values; continuous effect sizes and p-values, no NaN in comb_es or motif_fc (checked).

B5.why: 0 duplicate (TF, rsID, alt) rows in either assay (checked).

B6.why: Zenodo README describes files; column meanings deferred to the preprint and MIXALIME GitHub.

C1.why: In-vitro-to-in-cell transfer of allelic preference is informative whether it works or fails.

C2.why: Open general ASB predictors exist (AlphaGenome, IBIS models, PWMs), but none tested on these poorly characterized TFs.

C3.why: ASBs for ~150 previously motif-less TFs, only analysed so far by PWM concordance in the paper.

C4.why: Measuring allelic binding needs a ChIP-seq or GHT-SELEX experiment per TF in a heterozygous genome.

C5.why: Published 74% PWM concordance; my recomputed 67.5% (hit) and 53.3% (no hit) direction accuracy.

D1.why: DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer have open downloadable weights for DNA windows.

D2.why: Embed ~116k SNP windows x 2 alleles once on CPU, fit a small head on the difference.

D3.why: DNABERT-2 is Apache-2.0; data CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo record, checked).

E1.why: Hold out whole chromosomes (chr column present) and, separately, whole TFs.

E2.why: 22 chromosomes and 155 ChIP TFs; 53 TFs with >=20 significant ASBs (checked).

E3.why: Majority allele (52.3% ref) and PWM sign baseline computable from the files (checked).

E4.why: Per-replicate ref/alt counts in list columns allow replicate agreement estimates (checked).

E5.why: Strong motif-disrupting ASBs should reproduce ~74% PWM concordance; ChIP vs GHT-SELEX agree 71% on 38 shared ASBs.

E6.why: Shuffle alleles within TF, ablate motif features; straightforward on this table.

E7.why: ADASTRA, an independent ASB database from thousands of public ChIP-seq runs, covers the ~39 control TFs.

E8.why: 1,682/2,260 concordance reproducible from motif_fc and pref_allele columns.

G1.why: dbSNP rsIDs, hg38 coordinates and HGNC gene symbols in every row (checked).

G2.why: ADASTRA (rsID + TF), GTEx eQTLs and GWAS Catalog (rsID) are specific partners.

G3.why: One row per TF-SNP-allele; triallelic SNPs already split into biallelic records.

G4.why: Paper already tested GTEx/GWAS enrichment; a model adds variant scoring beyond HEK293 SNPs.

H1.why: 277k non-significant candidate SNPs recorded alongside 12,060 significant ASBs (checked).

H2.why: One genome (HEK293), one cell line, overexpressed tagged TFs; only HEK293 heterozygous SNPs.

H3.why: Claim is precise: allelic preference at HEK293 heterozygous SNPs for these TFs.

H4.why: Paper explicitly states ASBs are limited to SNPs present in HEK293 cells.

I1.why: Codebook consortium (Hughes lab, Kulakovskiy/autosome.org) and regulatory variant interpretation groups.

I2.why: Better scores would reprioritise candidate causal variants, but only marginally for most users.

I3.why: Direction accuracy is exactly the question 'which allele does this TF prefer'.

I4.why: 73% of significant ChIP ASBs lack a motif hit; may be linked variants, not learnable signal.

J1.why: Real modelling: DNA embeddings, grouped splits, in vitro to in vivo transfer.

J2.why: Motif logic gives sanity checks, but chromatin/linkage effects are hard to judge alone.

J3.why: PWM-baseline reproduction plus per-TF accuracy table is shareable even if models fail.

J4.why: Roughly two weeks suggested; not formally committed.

J5.why: Kill condition written in success_criteria; date not yet in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: Codebook PWMs (this paper) scored with PERFECTOS-APE
existing_models.score_and_split: 74% (1,682/2,260) direction concordance on strongly motif-disrupting ASBs, no training split (motifs from same data); my recompute 67.5% on all 2,809 ChIP ASBs with hits, 53.3% on no-hit ASBs.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: ASBs without a PWM hit may be linked marker variants acting indirectly; detected ASBs are limited to HEK293 SNPs.

existing_models.name: IBIS Challenge 2024 models (Codebook/GRECO-BIT crowdsourced benchmark)
existing_models.score_and_split: Best deep models slightly beat PWMs on held-out Codebook experiments and on regulatory SNP annotation (per bioRxiv 2025.11.16.688692 abstract; numbers not retrieved).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Huge platform-specific effects and overfitting risk across assays.

existing_models.name: AlphaGenome (DeepMind, Nature 2025/26)
existing_models.score_and_split: Matches or beats external models in 25 of 26 variant-effect evaluations (abstract); TF tracks come from ENCODE, so coverage of Codebook TFs is unverified.

existing_models.name: ASB benchmark of TF binding models (Genome Biology 2024, s13059-024-03424-2)
existing_models.score_and_split: 132,000 candidate ASB variants across 101 TFs; deep learning methods best (abstract only).

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 (DNA language model) embeddings of ref vs alt windows; Nucleotide Transformer as alternative

integration.partner_dataset: ADASTRA v6.1 allele-specific binding database (and GTEx v8 eQTLs)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Can allelic preferences learned from in vitro binding of poorly characterized TFs explain allele-specific binding and expression effects in other cell types that motifs of well-known TFs miss?

controls.positive_control: Reproduce the paper's 74% PWM concordance on strongly motif-disrupting ASBs; ASBs with large PWM score change must be the easiest predictions.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle ref/alt preference within TF and confirm accuracy falls to ~52% (majority allele); random-noise embeddings.
controls.external_validation: ADASTRA ASBs for the ~39 control TFs from independent public ChIP-seq; within-study, train on GHT-SELEX ASBs and test on ChIP-seq ASBs.

honest_claim_h3: The model predicts which allele a given TF binds more strongly at common SNPs heterozygous in HEK293 cells, measured by read imbalance in overexpression ChIP-seq or GHT-SELEX, and says nothing directly about other genomes or cell types.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around a common genetic variant to predict which version of the variant a little-studied transcription factor binds more strongly.
plain_idea.train_on: For each of ~155 transcription factors, the DNA window around each tested variant in both versions; 301,079 factor-variant pairs, 12,060 with a significant preference (verified).
plain_idea.predict: Which allele the factor prefers and by how much; the truth comes from counting sequencing reads carrying each allele in binding experiments on cells (ChIP-seq) or on extracted DNA (GHT-SELEX).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Geneticists ranking candidate causal variants could score variants for ~150 factors that had no binding model before; even failure tells us whether no-motif imbalances are real binding or linked noise.

more_or_better_data.why: Covers ~150 poorly characterized TFs largely absent from ADASTRA/ENCODE, but only 12,060 significant ASBs versus ADASTRA's >500,000 entries and the 132,000-variant Genome Biology benchmark.

confidence_score.why: Per-replicate allele counts and FDR allow per-variant uncertainty, but I did not check whether AlphaGenome or IBIS models already report calibrated confidence.

models_beatable.why: The PWM baseline is weak on no-hit ASBs (53.3% direction accuracy, computed); AlphaGenome (2025, large pretrained model) is strong but may lack tracks for these TFs, unverified.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new data joins that measures the same quantity the same way on the same split; ADASTRA is a different pipeline on different cell lines.

label_elsewhere.sources: ADASTRA allele-specific binding database (known resource; Nat Commun 2021 retrieved, 'more than half a million entries'); Genome Biology 2024 ASB benchmark set (132,000 variants, 101 TFs, retrieved abstract).
label_elsewhere.why: ADASTRA gives an independent test of the control TFs and extra training labels, though mostly for well-studied TFs.

risks: Codebook PWMs (and motif_fc) were learned from the same peaks that contain these SNPs, so motif features carry information from the test data.
All rows share one genome: the same SNP is tested for many TFs, so open-chromatin or copy-number effects at a locus leak across TFs in a random split.
Nearby SNPs in linkage share read imbalance; neighbouring variants split across train and test inflate accuracy.
Reference-mapping bias (52.3% of significant ChIP ASBs prefer ref) could be learned as a shortcut.
leakage_plan.split: Leave-chromosome-out (hold out whole chromosomes using the #chr column, seen in files), with a second evaluation holding out whole TFs (TF column, seen); never use motif_fc as a model input.
checks: Shuffle pref_allele within TF and confirm accuracy collapses to ~52%.
Train on locus-only features (no TF, no alleles) and confirm near-chance direction accuracy.
Report accuracy separately for variants with and without a motif hit, and versus distance to the nearest training SNP.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: chromosome hold-out handles the shared-genome and linkage problems, provided motif features are kept as baselines only.

success_criteria.metric: Direction accuracy (fraction of significant ASBs where the predicted preferred allele matches the observed one) on held-out chromosomes, reported separately for no-motif-hit ASBs, because the user decision is 'which allele disrupts binding'.
success_criteria.baselines: Majority allele 52.3% (ChIP, computed); Codebook PWM sign 67.5% on hit ASBs and 53.3% on no-hit ASBs (computed from files); published 74% on strongly motif-disrupting ASBs.
success_criteria.success: Direction accuracy >= 62% on no-hit ChIP ASBs and >= 72% on hit ASBs on held-out chromosomes, versus 53.3% and 67.5% for PWMs.
success_criteria.noise_ceiling: ChIP-seq and GHT-SELEX agree on direction for 71% (27/38) of ASBs significant in both (computed); replicate agreement not yet computed.
success_criteria.kill: Stop if after one week no-hit direction accuracy stays below 57% on held-out chromosomes for every model, meaning no-hit ASBs are mostly linked or indirect.

ambitious.why: Publishes variant-effect benchmarks; would need a clear gain over PWMs and AlphaGenome on held-out chromosomes plus ADASTRA transfer.

realistic.why: Fits a focused analysis of how well in vitro binding models predict allele-specific binding for newly characterized TFs.

fallback.why: A negative result (no-hit ASBs are unpredictable) with the reproduced PWM baseline is still a useful short note.

pitch.headline: 12,060 measured allele-specific binding events for ~190 transcription factors, ~150 of which had no binding motif before, in one clean CC-BY table.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Same HEK293 genome assayed both in cells (ChIP-seq, 10,575 ASBs) and on naked DNA (GHT-SELEX, 1,485 ASBs), with 289,657 tested non-significant candidates as negatives and per-replicate read counts.
pitch.the_win: Lift direction accuracy on the 7,766 no-motif-hit ChIP ASBs from the PWM's 53.3% to at least 62% on held-out chromosomes.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn whether most allele-specific binding without a motif hit is sequence-predictable or reflects linked variants and chromatin context, with a reproduced PWM baseline per TF.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Codebook/GRECO-BIT consortium (Hughes and Kulakovskiy groups) and ADASTRA maintainers deciding how to score variants for newly characterized TFs.

ml_idea: Embed ref and alt DNA windows (e.g., 200 bp) around each candidate SNP with a frozen DNA language model, add TF identity or TF-specific heads, and predict allelic preference; compare to Codebook PWMs and test transfer from GHT-SELEX (in vitro) to ChIP-seq (in cells) and to ADASTRA.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: ~116k unique SNPs x 2 alleles at ~30 short windows/s for DNABERT-2 on CPU; tables (40 MB) load in seconds (observed).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Train a simple k-mer or embedding classifier on 10 TFs with the most ASBs and check no-hit direction accuracy on held-out chromosomes beats 53.3%.

verdict_reason: Clean, verified ASB table (counts match the paper exactly) with a weak PWM baseline on no-motif ASBs, but one genome and thin per-TF counts; verify that no-hit ASBs carry learnable sequence signal before investing.
